[There's also a counter petition](https://www.change.org/p/centurytel-parents-with-working-brains-petition-to-help-keep-8-year-olds-with-stupid-parents-out-of-the-deadpool-movie)

This is stupid for many good reasons. Not the least of which being that even a PG-13 version of the character would not be appropriate for an 8 year old.

Deadpool is a psychopath. He is a literal insane person who has hallucinations, murders people for money, and has a filthy, filthy mouth and a dirty perverted mind. He is not for children and he has literally said this himself in his own comic book. He's fun for grown ups because he's whimsical and fun while doing these things, but is in no way appropriate for an eight year old even at a lesser MPAA rating.

Deadpool is not a super hero, he's a crazy person in spandex who kills people for money and because he's insane. He makes Frank Castle [the Punisher] seem morally grounded and sane.

I doubt the studio actually cares about this petition. At least on the level of considering giving in to it. Especially considering R rated comic movies are anything but rare, and are often successful films [and sometimes flops].

Examples: Blade, 300, V for Vendetta, The Crow, Kickass, Dredd, Sin City, American Splendor, Ghost World, Constantine, Kingsman, 30 Days of Night, Tank Girl, and Wanted. Many of these films also have sequels or reboots that are also R rated.

Many of these films are movies the kid should probably watch...when he's old enough. Deadpool is just one more to add to the shelf until he reaches that age. I don't get why the idea that the movie should be altered is even really a thing.

Anyway, this is dumb but seems worth discussing seeing as it's getting a lot of play on Youtube currently in the film review themed channels.

I'm against this, just because it's a stupid idea in general that wouldn't sanitize the movie enough for the intended purpose anyway.

Still, the petition has gotten some support, but it's also lost her subscribers and gotten a lot of downvotes. This seems more polarizing than seems to make sense given the character involved.

So what do we think of this? A PG-13 cut of Deadpool makes little sense to begin with, but the idea that petitioning studios this way seems kind of self absorbed to me and just seems like lazy parenting.
